correctness.rationale: For each theta in (1,2), the displayed branches are full onto and strictly expanding, and the paper source Proposition 4.1 supplies a W2,1 contraction with essential factor (1+theta/2)^(-2)<1. Convex combining yields uniform Doeblin Fortet bounds; compact W2,1→W1,1/L1 and L1 contraction yield uniform essential spectral radius <1. Every p has a strictly positive-probability full-branch component whose expanding inverse cylinders shrink, so positive eigenfunction modulus and equality in the positive triangle inequality force any peripheral phase to be constant; fixed modulus strictly positive inside via topological exactness. This proves eigenvalue1 simple and alone on unit circle; L1 contraction precludes Jordan chains. Norm-continuity and compact p then yield a uniform spectral gap and real-analytic normalized Riesz eigenprojection across [0,1]. Independent symbolic expansion of inverse weight yielded 2w(z)=a z-(3/4)a r z²+(5/8)a r² z³+..., and A C-B²=p(1-p)a0a1(r1-r0)² gives the stated Peano jet inversion and discriminant. The finite source verification only checks algebra, not operator spectra. Endpoint is Peano C1 data, not a claimed C3 density.
